Backlog item **b-08a36a**, tier 2, filed 2026-09-19 from PR #378. It recurred
in the spec loop's runs 39 and 45. Line numbers below were read at
`e8f5529e`.

**The hook reads the index.** `.pre-commit-config.yaml:100-107` declares the
`prose-limit` hook with `entry: uv run hooks/prose_limit.py` and
`pass_filenames: false`. With no arguments, `main` runs `commit_time`
(`hooks/prose_limit.py:215`). `commit_time` takes its file list from `staged`
(`:103`). `staged` lists `git diff --cached --name-status -M -z
--diff-filter=AMR` (`:53-58`). `commit_time` reads each file's staged blob
with `git show :<path>` (`:100-107`).

**`make check` runs that hook.** `Makefile:8-9` makes `lint` the single
command `prek run --all-files`, and `check` is `lint test` (`Makefile:18`).
Two consequences follow, and the item measured both.

- **An unstaged file is invisible.** An untracked file never reaches
  `staged`. The item measured a file after `git add -N` passing too, since
  that entry stages no content.
- **A staged file is read at its staged content.** After a refused commit,
  a copy fixed in the working tree still fails. The hits name lines it no
  longer has.

**prek cannot hand the hook the working tree.** `prek run --help` (prek
0.5.3) says `--all-files` runs hooks "on all tracked files". Measured
2026-10-20 in a scratch repo with a hook that echoes its arguments. It got
the tracked file and the intent-to-add file, and no untracked file. So the
hook lists its own files, and `pass_filenames` stays false.

**prek skips a manual-stage hook unless asked.** Measured 2026-10-20 in a
scratch repo with prek 0.5.3 and a hook declaring `stages: [manual]`. Plain
`prek run --all-files` did not run it. `git commit` with the pre-commit hook
installed did not run it either, with an untracked file present. Then
`prek run --all-files --stage manual <id>` ran that hook alone.
`prek run --all-files --stage manual` with no id ran every hook, since a hook
with no `stages` runs at every stage. `prek run --all-files --skip <id>`
reported that hook `Skipped`.

**A file mode exists and reads one file.** `--file <path>` reads the working
copy against `HEAD` (`hooks/prose_limit.py:144-169`), for both gates in
`GATES` (`:138`). It takes one path, and nothing in `make check` calls it.

**Who reads `make check`.** `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md:85-86` tells a spec
author to run `make check` before pushing a spec. CI runs
`uvx prek run --all-files` on a clean checkout (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:18`),
where nothing is staged or unstaged. `CLAUDE.md:228-230` says the
no-argument mode reads the staged index. That stays true here.

Add a third mode, `python3 hooks/prose_limit.py --tree`. It asks the
commit mode's question of the working tree instead of the index. It reads every
in-scope file the working tree adds, modifies or renames against `HEAD`,
staged or not. It also reads every untracked file git does not ignore. Each is
read at its working-tree content. Its baseline is the `HEAD` copy, or the old
path's `HEAD` copy for a rename git detects, or zero for a new file. It runs
the `prose` gate alone, as the commit mode does
(`hooks/prose_limit.py:108`). It prints in the commit mode's format and
exits 1 on any new hit, else 0.

Wire it into `make check`. Add a local hook to `.pre-commit-config.yaml` that
runs the tree mode at the manual stage only, with `always_run: true`. Change
the `lint` recipe in `Makefile` to call prek twice. The first call runs
`prek run --all-files` skipping `prose-limit`. The second runs the manual
stage with the new hook's id alone. The second call runs even when the first
fails, so a ruff failure cannot hide a prose hit. The recipe still exits
non-zero when either fails. Keeping the first call's status in a shell
variable does this in one recipe line, written as `$$` for make.

Leave the commit mode as it is. `prose-limit`'s config entry stays unchanged,
and the no-argument mode keeps reading the index. The per-commit limit
belongs there.

Add two sentences to `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` after the `make check`
sentence at `:85-86`. The first says `make check` reads each changed file's
working-tree copy, staged or not, while the commit hook reads the index. The
second says a file moved with plain `mv` reads against zero there until
`git add -A` stages the rename.

## Out of scope

- **The `terms` rules in tree mode.** The commit mode runs `prose` alone,
  and the `terms` hook already scans the tree (`.pre-commit-config.yaml:41-52`).
- **A rename git cannot see.** A file moved with plain `mv` and never staged
  shows as a deletion and an untracked file. Tree mode reads the new path
  against zero, so its old hits fail `make check`. No witness drives it, and
  the claim names only `git mv`. The `issue-tracker.md` sentence names the
  fix, `git add -A`.
- **CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:18` keeps `prek run --all-files`. A clean
  checkout has no working-tree change for the tree mode to read.
- **Two sentences this change makes false.** `CLAUDE.md:30` says
  `lint = prek run --all-files`. `.claude/skills/create-saffron-spec/SKILL.md:73-75`

  forbidden here. The delegate edits them in a review commit on this cell's
  pull request. The new wording says only the `prose-limit-tree` hook reads
  the working tree. The `--all-files` hooks still read tracked files only.
- **`.claude/agents/spec-writer.md`.** It stays true as written, and it is
  forbidden here.
- **A file staged as added, then deleted from the working tree.** Neither
  listing names it. Measured with git 2.54.0 and 2.47.3, for a file added
  with `git add`, one added with `git add -N`, and a `git mv` target, each
  then removed. So tree mode never reads it, and no witness drives it.

**Run the recipe without make.** The cell image has no `make` (measured

`anchored` and a `blocker` (`saffron/phases/review.py:787-794`).
`review_state` routes to REBUT only on what that returns
(`saffron/phases/review.py:863-880`). REBUT's own blocker list is the same

`_not_covered` lists its result (`saffron/report/pr_body.py:566-573`).

## Problem

The host ran a survivor's edit and watched the witness stay green. Anchoring
exists to drop a lens's hallucinated or off-diff finding. A host-filed
survivor is neither, yet anchoring decides whether it reaches REBUT. The
operator chose the first arm of the item's *Done looks like*. A host-filed
survivor reaches REBUT whether or not it anchors. A lens's finding keeps
today's rule.

1. **The rule.** `anchored_blockers` selects every blocker that anchors,
   and every blocker whose claim starts with `HOST_FILED`, in one pass in
   review order. Its docstring says why a survivor is exempt.
   `review_state`'s docstring says the same in one clause.

## Context

Backlog item **b-8a0c9a**. A stack batch's end review grades the heads
PACKAGE pushed. The delegate's review commits land after PACKAGE, so the
end review grades code the loop already changed. Runs 32, 33, 35, 44 and
45 each found most of its findings fixed on the branches by then. Two
follow-ups cost $6.06 in run 32 and both were wasted.

The operator chose a separate finish command. A `--stack` batch gains a
way to end after its order drains without running the end review. A new
`saffron finish <batch id> --repo .` later runs the end review on each
layer's current branch head, with the reserve the batch held. It then
runs the follow-ups and the finishing layer as the batch would have. The
work is split into five specs. This is the parent.

**`run_stack_batch` runs three callables after its order.** It hands
`end_review` the batch key, the reserve and a specs map. It calls
`end_review` whenever one is handed, whatever the stop reason
(`saffron/batch.py:852`, `:863`). It calls `follow_ups` only when one is handed (`:866`). It calls
`finish` only when one is handed (`:908-909`). The batch row closes after
all three. A `None` `follow_ups` needs nothing else, and a `None` `finish`
is skipped.

**`_batch` builds all three under `--stack`, once the scan resolves.** It
holds back `reserve_usd` and `writer_usd` through
`_stack_admission_shares(args.budget)` (`saffron/cli.py:2000-2001`). It
builds `_stack_end_review`, `_stack_follow_ups` and `_stack_finish` inside
the readiness and scan guard (`saffron/cli.py:2132`, `:2155`, `:2164`). It
hands them as `end_review=`, `follow_ups=` and `finish=`
(`saffron/cli.py:2214`, `:2219`, `:2221`). Each stays `None` when
readiness or the scan fails.

**The flag parser refuses a bad pairing with `error`.** `main` calls
`watch_parser.error` for a flag that needs another (`saffron/cli.py:279`,
`:281`). At base `saffron batch --defer-end-review` exits 2 with
`unrecognized arguments`, from the top parser, whose usage names no
`--stack` (measured on the host).

## Problem

Nothing lets a stack batch end before its end review. So no later command
can grade the heads the loop's review commits produce.

Add a `--defer-end-review` flag to `saffron batch`. Refuse it without
`--stack` through the batch parser's `error`, before the ledger opens.

Under both flags, build a deferring `end_review` callable beside where
`_stack_end_review` is built today, and hand it in that one's place. Hand
`follow_ups=None` and `finish=None`. Leave every other keyword as it is,
so the order still holds back the reserve and the writer's share.

The callable writes `deferred.json` into `finish/<batch key>/` under the
batch tree (`out_dir`). That is the directory `_stack_finish` writes
`findings.json` into. It then prints the `saffron finish` line. The file
is the contract `SA-0305` reads. A write that raises is printed and
swallowed, as `_stack_end_review` swallows its own raise.

## Out of scope

  layer's current branch head. `SA-0303` makes qualification and the
  follow-up writer read the same heads.
- **Resuming the batch.** `SA-0304` lets `run_stack_batch` resume a closed
  stack batch's tail on its own batch id.
- **The command.** `SA-0305` adds `saffron finish <batch id> --repo .`.
- **Making deferral the default.** The operator kept the in-batch end
  review as the default (see the notes).
- **`DESIGN.md` \xa74.2.1, `CONTEXT.md` and the spec loop's skill.** The
  operator edits them by hand in this spec's pull request.
- **An `end_reviews` row for a deferred batch.** The deferring callable
  records none. `SA-0305` refuses a batch whose layers hold one, so a row
  written here would refuse every deferred batch. No witness drives it,
  because the batch rigs hold no layer.
- **`saffron/batch.py`.** It needs no change. A `None` `follow_ups` and
  `finish` already skip both.

## Context

PACKAGE pushed, before the loop's review commits land. `SA-0301` lets a
`--stack` batch end before its end review and write `deferred.json`.
`SA-0305` adds `saffron finish <batch id> --repo .`, which runs the end
review later. This spec gives that command the batch loop's own tail to
call. It is the fourth of the five specs `SA-0301`'s notes lay out.

**The tail runs inside the call that created the batch.**
`run_stack_batch` creates its row with `ledger.create_batch` at
`saffron/batch.py:829`. After the
order's `_drive` returns, it calls `end_review` (`:852-865`), then
`follow_ups` (`:866-869`). It drives their return only when the order's
own reason is `DRAINED` (`:872`). It then calls `finish` (`:908-909`) and
closes the row through `_stop` (`:910`). A raise closes the row
`INFRASTRUCTURE` in the `finally` (`:911-914`). `_stop` names each task
left in flight, promotes the reason to `INCOMPLETE` for one, then calls
`close_batch` (`:933-937`).

**`close_batch` writes the night's window.** It sets `status`,
`ended_at` and `spent_usd_est` in one update (`saffron/ledger.py:1283-1287`).
`DESIGN.md` \xa74.2.1 keeps the batch's window and stop reason in `batches`
for \xa76's morning queue (`DESIGN.md:498`).

**Four reads name the batch by the newest row.** `ledger.latest_batch_id()`
returns the highest `batch_id` (`saffron/ledger.py:1337-1345`).
`run_stack_batch` reads `latest_batch_id()` to attach a minted task's run
(`saffron/batch.py:594-596`) and to weigh a revision's budget
(`saffron/batch.py:747-751`). It also hands `end_review` and `follow_ups`
their key from `latest_batch_id()` (`:864`, `:868`). A finish run days later
sees a newer batch there.

**The follow-up pass starts from the order's state.** `record_layer`
reads `position` and `predecessor_task_id` (`saffron/batch.py:522-534`). `wrapped` reads
`predecessor` (`:557`) and the exempt set `layer_branches` (`:600-602`).
The order's pass sets all four. `consecutive_aborts` carries the order's
count into the follow-ups' `_drive` (`:894`).

## Problem

Nothing can run a closed stack batch's tail on that batch's id.

Add a frozen dataclass `StackResume` to `saffron/batch.py`. Its fields are
`batch_id: int`, `budget_usd: float`, `stop_reason: StopReason`,
`top: Candidate`, `position: int`, `layer_branches: frozenset[str]` and
`specs: Mapping[str, Spec]`. Add `resume: StackResume | None = None` to
`run_stack_batch`'s keywords.

With a resume, `run_stack_batch` checks the three cases of criterion 5
first. It creates no row and drives no order. Its batch id is
`resume.batch_id`, and its reason starts as `resume.stop_reason`. The
follow-up pass starts from `resume.top` as the predecessor,
`resume.top.task_id` as the predecessor task, `resume.position` and
`set(resume.layer_branches)`, with no standing aborts. `end_review` gets
`resume.specs` in place of the specs built from the order. Every read of
`ledger.latest_batch_id()` in `run_stack_batch` becomes the batch id it
holds, with or without a resume.

**A resume never writes the batch row.** The row keeps the night as it
closed: its `status`, `ended_at` and `spent_usd_est`. A resume calls
neither `close_batch` nor `_stop`, on its return or on a raise. It
returns the tail's reason to its caller, which prints it. That reason is
the follow-ups' `_drive` reason when they are driven, else
`resume.stop_reason`. It takes `_stop`'s in-flight promotion and prints
`_stop`'s `left in flight` lines. Split that part of `_stop` into a
helper both call, so `_stop` stays the single call to `close_batch`.
Follow-ups are driven only when `resume.stop_reason` is `DRAINED`.

**Four texts in `saffron/batch.py` go false, so edit them.** The comment
above `finish` says it runs "while the batch row is still open"
(`:462-463`). Under a resume the row is closed. `run_stack_batch`'s own
docstring says the tail from `end_review` on runs "before the row
closes" (`:475-476`). Keep
that docstring within ten lines. The `generation` comment says it is set
"once the order's own pass drains" (`:507-509`). Under a resume no order
runs. `_stop`'s docstring says `run_stack_batch` calls it once, and in
its `finally` on a raise (`:930-932`). A resume calls it never.

## Out of scope

- **`saffron finish` itself**, reading `deferred.json` and the ledger, and
  building the adapters. `SA-0305` does that and calls this.
- **Grading current heads.** `SA-0302` and `SA-0303`.
- **`saffron/ledger.py`.** It is `elevate_on`, so this spec adds no
  accessor. `latest_batch_id`'s docstring says `run_stack_batch` reads it
  (`saffron/ledger.py:1338-1340`). That goes false here, and the delegate
  edits it in a review commit. `create_batch`'s docstring
  (`:1248-1252`) stays true, since a resume never closes a row.
- **`write_stack_view`'s own `latest_batch_id()`**
  (`saffron/report/stack.py:272`). It is `cli.py`'s call, after the batch.

## Notes for the agent

**New code, so no criterion declares a mutant.** The resume path does not
exist at base. `witness` will report `skip` for criteria 1 to 5. The
`latest_batch_id()` reads change no behaviour without a resume, which the
five `preserves` witnesses hold.

**What `SA-0305` must source, and refuse.** `deferred.json` (`SA-0301`)
holds `batch_id`, `reserve_usd`, `writer_usd` and `specs`. The rest come
from the ledger.

  `stop_reason` is the row's `status`, which has none. `SA-0305` reads it
  through `ledger._db`.
- `top` and `position` are the highest row of `ledger.stack_layers`, with
  `top.spec` taken from `specs`. The runner reads only
  `predecessor.spec.id` (`saffron/cli.py:698`).
- `layer_branches` is `_branch(spec_id)` of each layer, the form
  `record_layer` adds (`saffron/batch.py:534`). It also holds the stack base's branch.
  That is `tasks.branch` of the task whose `record_key` is the position 1
  row's `predecessor_key`, read through `ledger._db`. It is not
  `_branch(spec_id)`.
- `SA-0305` refuses a batch id with no `batches` row, as a folded ledger
  has. It refuses a batch with no layer, which has no `top`.

**Why `status` and not the order's own reason.** The row holds `_stop`'s
result (`saffron/batch.py:917-937`). It turns a drained order that left a task in flight
into `INCOMPLETE`. The in-batch path gates on `_drive`'s reason being
`DRAINED` before that turn (`:872`). So a deferred `INCOMPLETE` batch drives no
follow-ups on resume, where the in-batch path would have. This is a
deliberate, conservative difference. Criterion 2 drives `INCOMPLETE` and
criterion 1 drives `DRAINED`.

**`until`.** The tail meets only the `until` its caller hands. The row's
`until_ts` is not read. The in-batch end review runs after an `UNTIL`
stop too, so a resume after one still runs its end review.

**The row after a resume.** It reads as the night closed it, whatever
the tail does. A SIGTERM during a resume leaves it the same way. The
tail's spend still counts in `batch_spend`, which sums live rows
(`saffron/ledger.py:1364-1388`). Only the `spent_usd_est` snapshot omits it.
The stack view shows the live figure (`saffron/report/stack.py:93`).
`saffron serve`'s batch spend reads the `spent_usd_est` snapshot
instead (`saffron/view/graph.py:178-179`, `ontology/queries/view/V1-batches.rq`).
So after a resume it omits the tail's spend. The operator accepts that,
and the delegate files a backlog item for the view.

**The standing aborts are not carried.** The row holds no count, so the
follow-ups start at zero. A drained order ends with fewer than two.

- **The first** creates a later batch row with no spend after the

  and the resume's specs, and `follow_ups` the resumed id. Assert that
  `revise` never ran, and that `TE-31` alone ran, on `TE-2`. Assert its

- **The second** loops over the four reasons, a fresh helper batch each.

- **The third** loops over the three callables with the original reason

- **The fourth** has the one follow-up's runner return `IMPLEMENTING`.

`saffron finish <batch id> --repo <repo>`, defaulting `--repo` to the
working directory as the other commands do. Its help says it reads each
branch at origin and pushes nothing, so the operator pushes review commits
first. `main` runs it through `_guarding_sigterm`, inside the handler that
turns an unexpected raise into `saffron:` and exit 2.

   `<batch tree>/finish/<batch id>/deferred.json`. Print one line starting
   `saffron: finish refused:` that names why, and return 2, in each case
   criterion 2 lists. The id on the command line is the batch's id
   throughout, so a file whose `batch_id` differs is refused. Compare the
   resolved `--repo` with the file's `repo` as paths. Run the readiness
   probe last, as `_batch` calls it, and refuse with its step and detail
   when it fails. An outage then stops the command before a lens writes
   an `error` row, which would refuse every later run. The probe's own
   `base_sha` is not read. The tail grades at the pinned base in the
   file.
2. **Build the resume.** `budget_usd` is `ledger.batch_budget`.
   `stop_reason` is the row's `status`, read through `ledger._db`. `top` is
   a `Candidate` for the highest `stack_layers` row. Its `spec` is the one
   `deferred.json` holds for that layer's spec id, its `task_id` is that
   layer's task, and its `spec_sha` is that task's. Its `path` is
   `Path("<spec id>.md")`. Nothing in the tail reads a predecessor's path,
   since the runner and the spec sessions read only `predecessor.spec.id`
   (`saffron/cli.py:677`, `:692`). `position` is that
   row's position. `layer_branches` is `scheduler._branch` of each layer's
   spec id, plus the stack base task's `branch` when the bottom layer has
   a `predecessor_key`. `specs` is every spec in `deferred.json`, each read

   over the file's specs. Print `finish: <reason>` and exit as `_batch`
   does for that reason.
5. **Four texts name the commands.**

     `saffron package` (`CLAUDE.md:64`).
   - `CLAUDE.md` says a `--stack` night runs its end review from its
     reserve (`:76-77`). Add that a night started with
     `--defer-end-review` defers it to `saffron finish`, which spends that
     reserve.

   - `saffron/cli.py`'s module docstring lists every subcommand

- **Pushing.** The command reads each branch at origin. The spec loop's

- **Retrying an end review that errored.** A batch with any `end_reviews`
